title: Incremental Recommendation via Causal Models
abstract: arXiv:2608.26804v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Recommendation impressions are a finite resource, hence delivering a recommendation to a user who would discover the content organically yields no incremental value and displaces other recommendations that could. We address this by extending an existing production recommendation model to a causal architecture using holdback data that is already collected as part of routine experimentation infrastructure, requiring no new data collection. A central challenge is that attribution windows differ between treated and holdback observations: treated users are attributed a stream within a short direct-response window, while holdback users are attributed organic streams over a multi-day window. This mismatch makes naive treatment-effect subtraction invalid. We resolve this with a dual-threshold targeting policy that delivers a recommendation only when the probability of a treated stream is high and the probability of organic stream is low. In a

translated_title: 基于因果模型的增量推荐
translated_abstract: 推荐展示是一种有限资源，因此，向本会自然发现内容的用户推送推荐不会带来增量价值，反而会挤占其他可能更有价值的推荐机会。我们通过将现有的生产推荐模型扩展为因果架构来解决这一问题，利用常规实验基础设施中已收集的保留数据，无需新增数据收集。一个核心挑战是处理组和保留组观测之间的归因窗口不同：处理组用户在短直接响应窗口内被归因于流媒体，而保留组用户则被归因于多天窗口内的自然流媒体。这种不匹配使得简单的处理效应减法无效。我们通过一种双阈值定向策略来解决，仅在处理流概率高且自然流概率低时推送推荐。在实验中...
tldr: 本文提出一种基于因果模型的增量推荐方法，利用已有的保留数据，通过双阈值策略解决归因窗口不匹配问题，从而优化推荐资源分配，避免向自然发现内容的用户推送无效推荐。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes an incremental recommendation method based on causal models, leveraging existing holdback data and a dual-threshold strategy to address attribution window mismatches, optimizing recommendation resource allocation by avoiding ineffective pushes to users who would discover content organically.
